title.text: Work zone devices and barricade stripes

why_how.text: Keep this rule in mind: Construction and maintenance work areas use traffic control devices to guide drivers and pedestrians safely through the work zone and to protect highway workers, and orange is the basic color of these devices.
Keep this rule in mind: The most common work zone devices are signs, barricades, drums, cones, tubes, flashing arrow panels and flagpersons.
Keep this rule in mind: Construction and maintenance signs notify drivers of unusual or potentially dangerous conditions in or near work areas, most are diamond-shaped and a few are rectangular.

Keep this rule in mind: Barricades, vertical panels, drums, cones and tubes are the channelizing devices most often used to alert drivers to work zone hazards and guide them through, and at night they often carry flashing or steady burning lights.

The diagonal stripes on a barricade or vertical panel point the way traffic should pass, with stripes sloping down to the right meaning bear right and stripes sloping down to the left meaning bear left. This matters because read the stripes like an arrow: the downward slope points the way to go.
Keep this rule in mind: Large flashing or sequencing arrow panels are used in work zones day and night to guide drivers into certain lanes and to show that part of the road ahead is closed.
Keep this rule in mind: Flagpersons stop, slow or guide traffic through work zones, wear orange vests, shirts or jackets, and direct traffic with red flags or stop and slow paddles.
